en.title: House of Harkness' Young Wanda Maximoff Redefines Marvel Magic
en.summary: A fresh take on the Scarlet Witch and Agatha Harkness lands in a standalone graphic novel. Discover a magical boarding school adventure perfect for both young readers and seasoned fans.
en.body:
Forget the multiversal chaos and the weight of prophecy for a moment. **Marvel Comics** is inviting readers back to school with **House of Harkness**, a vibrant graphic novel that reimagines a teenage **Wanda Maximoff** navigating the halls of a magical academy. This isn't the Scarlet Witch you might know from the big screen; this is a Wanda finding her footing, surrounded by familiar faces in entirely new contexts.

The story, penned by **Preeti Chhibber**, centers on Wanda attending an exclusive boarding school run by the formidable Harkness family. Alongside her, you'll find teen versions of **Agatha Harkness**, **Doctor Strange**, **Loki**, and **Nico Minoru**, among other magically inclined Marvel characters. The graphic novel, originally serialized on the Marvel Unlimited app, has now been collected into a standalone format by Marvel and Scholastic, making it an accessible entry point for a new generation of fans and a welcome addition for existing ones. The adaptation from a vertical mobile scroll to traditional comic panels has been handled with care, preserving the kinetic energy of the original while offering a cohesive reading experience.

## A Magical Boarding School Experience

The core appeal of **House of Harkness** lies in its charming character development and its infectious sense of fun. The narrative blends humor with genuine heart, exploring the dynamics between these young sorcerers as they learn, grow, and undoubtedly get into magical mischief. It offers a refreshing perspective on characters often burdened by immense power and complex histories, presenting them in a more relatable, coming-of-age light. The setting itself—a magical boarding school—provides fertile ground for classic tropes of friendship, rivalry, and self-discovery, all filtered through a distinctly Marvel lens.

## A Breath of Fresh Air for Fans

For fans seeking something a little different within the expansive Marvel universe, **House of Harkness** delivers. It stands out among the more offbeat offerings, providing a narrative that feels both familiar and novel. The decision to collect the series into a single graphic novel format means readers can devour the entire story in one sitting, a perfect quick read for mobile consumption or a cozy afternoon. The enthusiastic reception from early readers, including the sentiment that it felt like "a breath of fresh air," highlights its success in carving out its own unique space. This graphic novel is a testament to how beloved characters can be reinterpreted to resonate with contemporary audiences, proving that great storytelling knows no age limits.

## What's Next

With **House of Harkness** now available as a standalone graphic novel, readers can dive into this magical reimaging anytime. Further details on any potential future installments or related projects from **Preeti Chhibber** within this specific continuity have not yet been announced.

House of Harkness has heart and lovely character development alongside a ton of humor and fun. Along with some of the other offbeat offerings on Marvel Unlimited, it felt like a breath of fresh air. Now Marvel and Scholastic have  released  House of Harkness  as a standalone graphic novel , which means you can read the whole thing in one sitting. Someone did an amazing job of converting a comic that was created for a vertical scroll on your phone into something with panels on the page—there were only a few instances where the layouts felt a bit cramped, or something that had “popped” on my phone felt like it had less impact in the midst of other panels. Overall,  House of Harkness  is a lovely, quick read in graphic-novel format, and I highly, massively recommend picking it up. Your kids will love it, but so will you. In  House of Harkness , Wanda Maximoff is a teen witch who goes to an exclusive boarding school run by the Harkness family. She quickly sparks up a rivalry with the spoiled Agatha Harkness, but the two of them soon find themselves facing a bigger threat to the school. Because I adore this graphic novel so much, I decided to talk to writer Preeti Chhibber and artist Jodi Nishijima about how it came to be. Our Q&A is below. Where do you think this trend comes from? Why are these reimaginings popular? Preeti Chhibber : I think there’s joy in a coming-of-age story, and when you pair that with superheroes, you’ve got something golden.
